scope: loyalty_transactions schema, UNIQUE constraint analysis, FK integrity, append-only enforcement, indexing, branch-scoping

columns.name: balance_after
columns.type: INT NOT NULL — snapshot of user's loyalty_points after this txn

unique_keys: loyalty_transactions_user_order_type_unique = UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) — added in migration 2026_03_26_075919

findings.title: UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) is NULL-permissive — does NOT enforce earn-per-order uniqueness when order_id is NULL
findings.finding: MySQL (and most SQL engines) treat each NULL as distinct in UNIQUE constraints. UNIQUE(user_id, order_id=NULL, type='redeem') allows unlimited rows. Pre-order kiosk redemptions (LoyaltyController::redeem line 312, FrontendOrderService::createKioskLoyaltyRedeemLedger first attempt line 872 uses order_id=$this->frontendOrder->id but the LoyaltyController path uses NULL) and admin manual_add (LoyaltyController::addPoints line 224 uses order_id=null) bypass uniqueness entirely.
findings.impact: Double-redeem race in LoyaltyController::redeem (kiosk path before order persisted, manual_add by staff) cannot be DB-blocked. Only the lockForUpdate + balance-check at controller line 274-300 prevents overdraft — but UNIQUE provides no defense in depth.
findings.remediation: Option A: Add a deterministic synthetic key column (e.g. dedup_key VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '') populated via app-layer hash of (user_id|order_id|type|context|nonce) and UNIQUE(dedup_key). Option B (lighter): for manual_add and pre-order redeem, write a non-NULL placeholder pseudo-id (e.g. negative bigint derived from a UUID) into order_id. Option B has FK implications since order_id has no FK — feasible. Owner gate required.

findings.title: loyalty_transactions has NO branch_id column — analytics are global, not branch-scoped
findings.finding: Per BranchScope discipline (CLAUDE.md §9), all multi-tenant analytics tables should carry branch_id. loyalty_transactions does not. Analytics queries 'redeem in Branch A this month' must JOIN orders to derive branch — possible but slow, and impossible for order_id=NULL rows.
findings.remediation: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN branch_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NULLABLE AFTER user_id + index. Populate via backfill from orders. App-layer changes in listener + controller + service to set branch_id from $order->branch_id (or User::branch_id for manual_add).

findings.title: No append-only DB trigger on loyalty_transactions (UPDATE/DELETE not blocked)
findings.finding: Per CLAUDE.md §8, fiscal-grade tables (audit_logs, z_reports) have BEFORE DELETE triggers raising SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'. loyalty_transactions has none. App-layer comments call it 'immutable audit trail' (LoyaltyTransaction docblock line 8-15) but DB allows UPDATE/DELETE.
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth gap. An attacker with DB write access (or a buggy command) can rewrite history. Not NF525-required since loyalty is not fiscal — but it's money-equivalent (1€ discount = 100pts).
findings.remediation: Add migration with BEFORE DELETE and BEFORE UPDATE triggers (MySQL prod only — sqlite tests skip). Pattern available in existing audit_logs trigger migrations.

findings.title: No FK from loyalty_transactions.order_id → orders.id
findings.finding: order_id is indexed but not FK-constrained. Orphan rows (order deleted, txn remains) are possible. Since orders are soft-deletable in this codebase (verify), this might be intentional to preserve audit trail on hard delete — but if orders is purged, txn becomes orphan.
findings.remediation: Add FK with ON DELETE SET NULL — preserves txn audit even if order is purged. Or document intentional no-FK choice.

findings.title: users.loyalty_points is INT — overflow possible at ~21M points
findings.finding: Migration 2026_03_08_145926 declares loyalty_points INT (signed, ~2.1B max but Laravel INT default is signed 11-digit). For LeCayenne V1 single-resto this is far from a concern. Documented for V2 multi-resto scaling.

notes: PLOY-1-DBA-01 (NULL-permissive UNIQUE) is the main DB-layer defense gap. App-layer lockForUpdate compensates for the earn happy-path (UNIQUE INDEX prevents earn double-write — order_id is NOT NULL for earn). Concern primarily applies to redeem and manual_add paths.
